ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are two horizontal straight lines, upper and lower, and arrows in the same direction are used to mark them as parallel lines. In the middle there is a broken-line-shaped slanted line connecting these two parallel lines, with the vertex on the left side, the two slanted sides opening to the right, and the vertex is labeled as angle 1. The acute angle formed by the upper slanted line and the upper parallel line is labeled 36°, and the acute angle formed by the lower slanted line and the lower parallel line is labeled 31°. Then reason: Because the two horizontal lines are parallel, the horizontal reference line passing through the vertex of angle 1 can be regarded as being in the same direction as the upper and lower parallel lines. The angle of the upper slanted line relative to this horizontal reference line is 36°, and the angle of the lower slanted line relative to this horizontal reference line is 31°. Angle 1 is the angle opening to the right between these two slanted lines, so m∠1 = 36° + 31° = 67°.
